paper.title: Online Decision Deferral under Budget Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning-to-defer, bandit feedback (two-armed generalized linear contextual bandit with budget constraint)
unmapped: Two arms (ML model, human) with separate unknown parameters theta_m, theta_h in [0,1]^d; contexts shared across arms (no shared parameter)
Deferring to the human incurs a random generalized-linear cost c_t = mu(x^T w*) + noise with unknown w*; the model is cost-free
Context distribution satisfies lambda_min(E[x x^T]) > sigma_0 > 0
Link mu twice differentiable with first and second derivatives bounded by L_mu and M_mu
The learner knows the lower bound kappa on the link derivative (used in the confidence width beta(t))
settings.definition_quote: We model online learning-to-defer as a two-armed contextual bandit problem with budget constraints. ... in the \emph{Bandit} setting, the model's performance can only be observed when chosen, \textit{i.e.} $O_t=\{\pi(x_t)\}$. ... the reward is $r_{a,t}=\mu( x_t^\top \theta_a^*)+\eta_{a,t}$, where $\eta_{a,t}$ is a zero-mean, $\sigma-$sub-Gaussian martingale noise

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning-to-defer, full information (model performance always observed)
unmapped: Paper calls it 'full information', but only the model's reward is always observed; the human's reward and cost are observed only when deferring (mapped as a fixed directed feedback graph h -> m)
Two arms (ML model, human) with separate unknown parameters in [0,1]^d
Deferring to the human incurs a random generalized-linear cost with unknown parameter w*
Context distribution satisfies lambda_min(E[x x^T]) > sigma_0 > 0
Link mu twice differentiable with derivatives bounded by L_mu, M_mu
settings.definition_quote: \emph{Full information} is when the model's performance is always observable but the received reward is that of the chosen decision. The observation is $O_t=\{\text{m}, \pi(x_t)\}$ but reward is only $r_{\pi(x_t),t} $

algorithms.name: Generalized Linear Bandit with Budget Constraints (Algorithm 1, adapted from Agrawal & Devanur 2016)
NeuralLinear / NeuralLogistic variant (Algorithm 1 on learned embeddings)

symbols.OPT: value of the optimal static policy (Definition 3.1), satisfying budget in expectation

conditions: contexts i.i.d. with ||x||_2 <= 1 and lambda_min(E[x x^T]) > sigma_0 > 0
link mu twice differentiable, mu' <= L_mu, mu'' <= M_mu, kappa = inf mu' > 0
noise independent of context and action
tuning: initial random exploration for tau = O((d + log(1/delta))/sigma_0^2) rounds

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Under the setting presented in Section \ref{sec:model}, and assuming $B>d^{1/2}T^{3/4}$ Algorithm \ref{alg:glm} achieves regret $R_T = O\left((\frac{\text{OPT}}{B}+1)\frac{L_{\mu}d\sigma}{\kappa}  \sqrt{T \log \frac{T}{d\delta} \log \frac{T}{d}}\right)$ with probability $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Comparator is the optimal static policy satisfying the budget in expectation. L_mu mapped to k_mu, kappa to c_mu. Corollary A.5 in the appendix restates the same bound. Proof largely defers to Agrawal & Devanur (2016).
